name: Rowan Cheung / The Rundown AI
overview: The Rundown AI is the largest plain-English AI news media brand: a free daily newsletter ('Get the latest in AI in 5 minutes a day') founded by Canadian college dropout Rowan Cheung in early 2023, now surrounded by a multi-platform machine (X, Instagram, LinkedIn, short-form video) and an education upsell (Rundown University). It matters to @ac.wins because it is the category-defining proof that 'AI explained simply, daily' can scale from a solo creator to an 8-figure-adjacent media business, and its playbook — daily digestible AI news on social driving an owned email list, then monetizing via sponsors and a paid education tier — is the grown-up version of the funnel @ac.wins is building toward consulting.
key_metrics: [uncertain] Newsletter subscribers: ~2M active (company claims 2M+ 'early adopters'; 2.6M active subscribers cited alongside the Electrify investment news, as of mid-2026); 1.4M cited in an early-2026 analyst breakdown — figures conflict across sources

Revenue: $3M booked in 2024; ~$7M projected for 2025 (Forbes); reported first AI newsletter to hit ~$10M/year run-rate by late 2025 / early 2026 (2.8 years after launch), i.e. ~$7 revenue per subscriber per year vs ~$0.25-0.35 for typical AI newsletters
Newsletter open rate: 50-52% average (industry-leading; ~51.7% cited on ad marketplace as of 2026); ~2.5% click rate
Social following: @therundownai Instagram ~551K followers; Rowan's personal @rowancheung Instagram ~452K; X ~590K+; 1.5M+ total social followers claimed across accounts (as of 2025-2026)
Instagram growth: +160K followers in roughly one year attributed to an AI-avatar short-form video workflow (as of ~2025)
Early growth benchmark: 0 to 150K newsletter subscribers and 1K to 250K Twitter followers in the first 4 months (2023); ~2,500 new members/day average in first 3 months

[uncertain] Education: AI training delivered to 63K+ professionals and companies; Rundown University ~$1,000/yr (listed ~$84/month billed annually), reportedly approaching 50% of revenue (as of late 2025 / 2026; revenue-share figure from a single third-party analysis)
Sponsors include Google, Salesforce, Amazon; 2-3 labeled sponsor placements per issue; ads booked out months in advance (as of 2026)
Funding: bootstrapped until a strategic investment from Electrify (creator-backing firm behind Veritasium, Fireship), announced 2026
data_recency: Mostly as of 2025-07 through 2026-07 (Forbes profile, ad marketplace listings, Electrify investment coverage). Follower and subscriber counts go stale within months at this brand's growth rate; revenue figures are annual projections and stable for ~a year.
tactics_that_work: Simplify-and-summarize positioning: find the latest AI developments, strip jargon, and publish them in skimmable plain English 'anyone can understand' — identical positioning to @ac.wins but at news speed. This was the core engine of 0-to-150K in 4 months.

Social-to-email flywheel: viral X threads with a one-line CTA to the newsletter at the bottom of every thread; first 55K subscribers came organically from Twitter alone. Social builds reach, email owns the audience, and email then promotes new social surfaces.
Platform-native repackaging: threads are deliberately shorter and shallower than the newsletter ('Twitter users don't like to read that much'); same story, different depth per surface.

AI-avatar video cloning: Rowan cloned his own face and voice with AI to turn written news items into Reels/Shorts without filming, adding ~160K Instagram followers in about a year — a solo-founder-feasible way to be 'on camera' daily.
Design and skimmability as a moat: heavy investment in newsletter formatting (sections, visuals) so a 5-minute read feels effortless; cited by beehiiv as a key differentiator.
Embedded subscribe widgets on owned side-projects: a beehiiv embed on his Supertools AI-tool database drove ~10K newsletter signups.
Automating the back office with AI: sponsorship sales and parts of production are automated, keeping the team tiny relative to revenue.

Laddered monetization: free daily news (top of funnel) -> premium sponsors (monetize reach) -> $1K/yr Rundown University (monetize trust), with education reportedly approaching half of revenue — de-risking the ad-dependent model.
content_formats: Daily email newsletter (flagship, sectioned 5-minute read with graphics); X threads and single posts (short, punchy digests); Instagram Reels and Shorts produced via AI avatar (face/voice clone reading scripted news); Instagram feed posts on @therundownai; LinkedIn reposts; workshops and guides inside Rundown University. Short-form video is the fastest-growing surface (+160K IG followers/yr); email remains the monetization core with 50%+ open rates.
posting_cadence: Newsletter daily (weekdays); social multiple posts per day on X; Reels/Shorts near-daily via the avatar workflow.
hooks_and_copy_style: Urgency + simplicity: 'Get the latest in AI in 5 minutes a day.' Hooks lead with the newest model/tool name and a concrete capability or number, then a plain-English 'why it matters' line. Threads open with a bold claim about the news item, use short line-broken sentences, minimal jargon, and end with a soft CTA to the free newsletter. Newsletter uses labeled sections (news, tools, tutorials, 'why it matters') so every item has a takeaway. Tone: enthusiastic early-adopter, never academic.
monetization_model: Two engines: (1) newsletter sponsorships/advertising — 2-3 clearly labeled placements per daily issue sold to AI and enterprise brands (Google, Salesforce, Amazon), historically ~100% of revenue; (2) Rundown University — paid education membership (~$1,000/yr) with workshops, guides and certifications, reportedly approaching 50% of revenue by late 2025/2026. No consulting arm; monetization is media + courses at scale.
offer_and_pricing: Free daily newsletter (the core offer). Rundown University: ~$84/month billed annually (~$1,008/yr) for AI workshops, guides, certifications, community. Sponsorships: pricing gated behind a sales form (quote within 24h); ad inventory booked out months ahead; marketplace listing advertises 2M+ subscribers, ~51.7% open rate, 2.5% CTR. [uncertain] exact current sponsorship price per placement (not public; comparable large AI newsletters charge five figures per send).
audience_profile: Self-described '2M+ early adopters' — a broad prosumer audience of professionals, operators and enthusiasts who want to keep up with AI, skewing tech-curious knowledge workers rather than SMB owners specifically. Corporate training buyers (63K+ professionals trained) indicate meaningful B2B/enterprise reach. Overlap with @ac.wins ICP (non-tech business decision-makers) is partial: Rundown serves them news, not implementation — leaving the 'do it for me / show my business how' layer open.
funnel_map: X thread or Reel (AI-avatar news clip) -> CTA to free newsletter (link in bio / thread footer / embed on Supertools) -> daily email builds habit and trust -> in-email house ads promote Rundown University ($1K/yr) and workshops -> sponsors pay to ride the same emails. Email is the hub; social surfaces are interchangeable acquisition spokes. No DM automation or call-booking layer — it is a media funnel, not a services funnel.
proof_and_credibility: Subscriber count worn as the headline proof ('read by 2,000,000+'); named mega-sponsors (Google, Amazon, Salesforce) as social proof; Forbes profile and press coverage; '63K+ professionals trained' for the education arm; Rowan's personal brand as 'one of the most-followed AI educators worldwide'; consistent daily shipping since 2023 as implicit reliability proof. No client case studies — scale itself is the proof.
takeaways_for_ac_wins: Copy the flywheel shape, not the scale: every @ac.wins Reel and carousel should end with one consistent CTA into an owned channel (email or WhatsApp/broadcast list), because Rundown's first 55K subscribers came purely from social posts with a one-line CTA. Start the list now at sub-10K followers.

Adopt 'why it matters for your business' as a mandatory final beat in every daily one-stat post — Rundown's plain-English 'why it matters' framing is the single most copied element of its style and fits AC's black-and-gold stat format perfectly.

Use the AI-avatar workflow selectively: Rowan added ~160K IG followers in a year by cloning his face/voice to ship daily video. A solo HK consultant can do a lighter version (voice clone + branded motion graphics) to sustain daily Reels without filming — but keep some genuinely human on-camera moments for trust, since AC sells consulting, not media.

Differentiate on depth, not speed: Rundown wins the 'what happened in AI today' race. @ac.wins should not compete on news velocity; instead translate the same news into 'here is what a HK restaurant/clinic/agency should do about it' — the implementation layer Rundown deliberately leaves open.

Plan a productized mid-tier: Rundown's ~$1K/yr University shows plain-English AI education monetizes at ~50% of revenue. AC can mirror this small: a low-hundreds-USD workshop or template pack between free content and bespoke consulting, smoothing the jump to ac-wins.com engagements.
risks_or_avoid: Do not copy the ad-supported media model at sub-10K followers — sponsorship economics only work at six-figure reach. Avoid the pure-aggregator trap: @ac.wins summarizing the same news as Rundown (2M subscribers, faster, bigger team) is a losing head-to-head; only the localized implementation angle wins. Daily news cadence is a treadmill — missing days breaks the promise, and a solo consultant with client work will struggle to match it; a 'daily stat' is more sustainable than 'daily news.' AI-avatar content at high volume risks feeling synthetic and eroding the personal trust a consulting funnel depends on.
platform_policy_risk: Moderate and instructive: Rundown-style AI-avatar Reels fall squarely under Meta's 2025-26 AI-generated-content labeling, and news-summary content is exposed to originality/aggregator deprioritization since Instagram's 2025 originality updates penalize reposted or non-original material. Rundown mitigates via owned email (platform-independent). For @ac.wins: label AI-generated video honestly, add original commentary/analysis to every news-derived post so it is transformation rather than aggregation, and avoid identical templated slides day after day, which templated-content deprioritization can suppress.
discoverability_seo: Strong keyword discipline worth copying: post copy consistently contains high-intent AI keywords (tool names, model names, 'AI news') which now also surfaces in Google since Instagram professional-account content became Google-indexable (2025-07). Rundown additionally owns search real estate via therundown.ai and side sites (Supertools). For @ac.wins: put the tool/stat keyword in the first caption line and on-image text, and mirror content to ac-wins.com pages so Google captures both the IG post and an owned page.
localization_language: English-only, globally aimed; no localization. This leaves Chinese-language plain-English-style AI education under-served — a HK-based bilingual (EN + Traditional Chinese) angle is clear differentiation for @ac.wins in HK/GBA/SEA markets that Rundown will not contest.
replicability_effort: The full model is not solo-replicable (Rundown now has a team, sales function, and 2M-subscriber compounding advantage). The replicable core costs roughly 5-8 hours/week: daily social post with newsletter/broadcast CTA (2-3 h/wk using AI drafting), a weekly plain-English email digest (1-2 h/wk on beehiiv free tier ~$0-40/mo), and an AI-avatar or voice-clone video pipeline (HeyGen/ElevenLabs, ~$30-100/mo, ~2 h/wk once templated). Total tooling under ~$150/month.
benchmark_targets: Directional benchmarks for @ac.wins (scaled to a sub-10K services account): email/broadcast open rate 45-50% (Rundown: 50-52%); email click rate ~2-2.5%; social-to-email conversion — Rundown converted roughly 0.6 newsletter subscriber per Twitter follower in year one, so target ~0.3-0.5 owned-list contacts per IG follower; consistency KPI: 5+ posts/week for 90 straight days (the habit that built Rundown); revenue-per-audience sanity check: Rundown earns ~$7/subscriber/yr from media — a consulting funnel should target far higher revenue per 1,000 followers (one $2K+ client per month per few thousand engaged followers) rather than chasing ad-model economics.
